preamble: The offglide of the diphthong /au/ became a labial fricative in post-classical Greek: /au/ > /aw/ > [aβ] > /av/, generalized by about the 4th century AD. Before voiceless consonants (/p t k f θ s x/) and word-finally the fricative is voiceless, giving Modern Greek [af]; before vowels and voiced consonants it is [av] (see au_to_v). The same development affected ευ (> [ef]/[ev]). The outcome is the sequence [af]: only the glide element becomes [f]. The change is confined to Greek.

examples.note: The offglide becomes voiceless [f] before voiceless /t/.
